narrative.text: The Tyvaren military buildup on the northern border has accelerated. Intelligence reports three divisions forward-deployed, with armored units positioned within striking distance of the Sevagrad corridor — the historical invasion route used in both 1918 and 1942. General Brenner has proposed a defensive fortification line: bunkers, anti-tank ditches, artillery emplacements, and a forward observation network stretching forty kilometers along the most likely approach routes.

Forty million ₭, six weeks to complete. The fortifications would make a Tyvaren armored advance through Sevagrad significantly more costly — not impossible, but costly enough to deter anything short of a full-scale invasion. I will be direct: this is not a peacetime infrastructure project. This is preparation for a war that may be coming whether we prepare or not. The Tyvaren military has forty T-62 tanks deployed to their western district. We have zero. The fortifications close some of that gap.

There is a diplomatic dimension. Fortifying the Sevagrad corridor will be seen by Tyvaren as a provocation and by the international community as escalation. Our Arcturian contacts have already indicated that 'excessive militarization' of the border could complicate the trade negotiations. On the other hand, if Tyvaren attacks and the corridor is undefended, the trade negotiations will not matter because there will be no Veltrian government to negotiate.
At week three of construction, the project will require a decision on the scale of fortification — full military defensive line versus limited defensive emplacements.

choices.text: "Build the fortifications. Forty million ₭ from the military budget and contingency reserves. General Brenner, you have six weeks. Dusek, prepare the diplomatic response — we are not militarizing a border, we are defending one. Tyvaren has forty tanks pointed at us. A defensive line is not provocation. It is prudence."

"Defer the fortifications for four weeks. Brenner, I want updated intelligence on Tyvaren force dispositions — are the three divisions fully operational or partially mobilized? Dusek, explore whether Arcturian diplomatic pressure on Tyvaren could reduce the threat level without fortifications. If the intelligence confirms imminent threat, we build. If not, we wait."

"I will not militarize the Tyvaren border while diplomatic channels remain open. Fortifications send a message of hostility that may become self-fulfilling. Brenner, focus on mobile defense capabilities rather than fixed positions — a flexible force is more useful than bunkers that may face the wrong direction. The military budget should prioritize readiness, not concrete."
